parts.headline: Nvidia’s Demand Is Real. Its Financing Is Fragile.
AI Spending Has Met Its First Real Bill

mentions.section: Long the chips, short the returns
mentions.excerpt: Quanta 72’s dot-com comparison adds a necessary correction.

Quanta 72 compares Cisco, EMC, Oracle and Sun with Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon and points to the difference: the dot-com suppliers depended on customers who could stop buying, while today’s spenders fund the buildout from advertising, cloud, software and e-commerce.

Quanta 72 added on September 27 that the notice lets Oracle delay payments if power delays push the campus past its 2028 start; Oracle has missed no payment, and Blue Owl calls its commitments unchanged.

sides.claim: Unlike dot-com era suppliers, today’s hyperscalers fund AI investment from profitable core businesses such as advertising, cloud, software, subscriptions, and e-commerce, so the question is not whether they can afford the spending.

The most important signal for AI-era investors is the relationship between capital spending, free cash flow, and the growth those investments eventually produce, because in the dot-com boom stock prices turned before earnings and cash flow collapsed.

On the same day the spread closed at 2.80%, Oracle sent a force majeure notice to Blue Owl Capital, developer of the Project Jupiter Stargate campus, covering potential cost increases and letting Oracle delay payments if the campus misses its 2028…
The current AI-related selloff is not evidence that AI itself has failed, but a moment where investors are demanding proof that the infrastructure buildout converts into proportional revenue.
